name: Segmented
summary: Switch between a few mutually-exclusive options inline — labels, leading icons, or icon-only, in three sizes.
lead: ONE custom element — <aha-segmented> — defined once, imported unchanged by React and Vue. The DS V3 Segmented is a family, not a flat pill row: each item is a label, a leading icon + label, or an icon-only glyph (an aria-label is then required); an option can be disabled, or the whole control disabled. Three `size`s (small · medium · large) drive the height/padding/font/radius; `block` stretches it full-width with flex-equal options. Shadow-DOM CSS, themed only by --aha-* tokens; selection slides a persistent thumb (transform on a node that is never rebuilt), so it animates. Zero drift — the same element, not two look-alikes.
codeNote: Same element, same shadow-DOM CSS → identical render. React (< 19) consumes it via a thin ref wrapper; Vue binds the custom element natively. The primitive is defined once in @ahaslides-product/design.

opinion.note: Keep labels to one word where possible and the option count small (2–4). Icon-only options MUST carry an aria-label. It is a single-select control — for a magnitude use Rate or a Slider.
opinion.dsv3: COVERED — enumerated from the DS V3 Segmented component-set taxonomy: Segmented-Group (the control), Segmented-Item (label · leading icon + label · icon-only, plus selected/disabled states), Form-Item/Segmented-radio. The family carries three sizes (small · medium · large), a block full-width mode, per-option and whole-control disabled, and icon-only items. Token layer: track gray-20, thumb bg-container white with a soft shadow, selected label text-default; radius from the 4/6/8/12 scale by size. The thumb is a persistent node moved by transform via the shared motion tokens — no subtree rebuild on select.

conformance.$about: Measured by qa.mjs against the RENDERED UI (getComputedStyle via headless CDP). Leaf = ONE shared element, single render. The probe holds value=week at the default (medium) size so a selected segment exists and the size-dependent height is measurable.
